  1. they are using the tactic of embrace, extend, extinguish with their software, adding so many nonstandard extensions (which people will use) that it becomes very difficult to implement one's own replacements, even if following the standard.
  2. example: gnu extensions to the c and c++ standard libraries (glibc) are used in most large programs (e.g. firefox, kde) which make it impossible to use other implementations of the c library (e.g. uclibc), even if said other implementations follow the standards to the letter.
  3. for example: in gnu coreutils (specifically the cat utility) they support -b (number non-blank lines), -s (compress blank lines) and other pointless switches whose functionality could easily be implemented using sed/awk/whatever -- however, script writers and even C programmers (through the use of exec() and system()) use these extensions, which is often a pita to replace.
